paragraphs: Our New Nature Corner. By Mia. The school library has a new corner for books about nature. Teacher Kim and the Explorers made it in two weeks. We worked after school on Thursdays, and every Explorer had a job. This post has headings, so you can find the facts easily. Look at the headings first.

What Is in the Corner. The corner is a quiet area next to the big window of the library. It has one bookshelf, two soft chairs, and a small table. The chairs are very comfortable, and you can sit for a long time. Leo made a green poster with the words "Nature Corner." May made a bookmark for every child who borrows a book. Lily wrote the rules, and they are on the wall next to the poster.

The Bookshelf. The bookshelf has three shelves, and each shelf has a color. The top shelf is green, and it has books about plants. The middle shelf is blue, and it has books about the sea. The bottom shelf is orange, and it has books about insects and birds. There are forty books on the bookshelf. Each book has a small sticker in the color of its shelf, so it is easy to put back. Photo by Mia: the bookshelf in the Nature Corner.

Lunchtime Reading. The corner is open daily at lunchtime. It opens at twelve o'clock and closes at one o'clock. Children can read there, and they can borrow two books for one week. A teacher is always in the corner, but you must be quiet. If you cannot find a book, ask the teacher for help. Books about animals are especially popular. The book about sharks is never on the shelf.

Adult Readers. The corner is for adults, too. The adults like the quiet area, because nobody talks loudly there. A parent can come at lunchtime and borrow a book. Every adult signs a small card at the library desk. On Wednesday, a parent reads a story to the youngest children. The children sit on the floor and listen.

A Successful Start. In the first week, sixty children came to the corner. Teacher Kim says, "The corner is successful, because the children love it." Leo wants a new shelf for comic books, and I want one for animal books. Which books do you want in the corner? Write your idea in a message!
